bounded_predicate: For a class/object whose syntactic super names contain Iterator, locate next and report the class/object name if no descendant throw has a direct call expression with callee text NoSuchElementException. No reachability, exhausted-state or delegated-call proof.

positive.intent: A valid Iterator implementation returns a sentinel after exhaustion. hasNext is side-effect-free: this is the next exhaustion contract, not the earlier hasNext-calls-next rule.

negative.intent: The same legal implementation explicitly throws the standard exhaustion exception before indexing. The selected rule stays active.

suppression.intent: Genuine file-scoped upstream suppression only on the package-isolated copy. Preserve every positive range from the byte-identical unsuppressed neighbor. No host finding filter or ktChecker-ID suppression alias.

controls.intent: The actual List iterator supplies next and its exhaustion exception. A local throw is unnecessary, but the shallow rule still reports; retain the anticipated false positive.

An uncalled local function contains the recognized throw while the exhausted execution path still returns a sentinel. Descendant presence is not reachability or contract proof; preserve the anticipated miss.

The live exhaustion guard throws the genuine fully qualified JDK exception. Its qualified-expression shape is not the direct KtCallExpression accepted by the predicate; retain this anticipated false positive.

limitations: This is a syntactic next-exhaustion warning, distinct from hasNext consuming the iterator. No existing hasNext case, count or identity is replaced.
Delegation and qualified exception names produce anticipated false positives; an uncalled nested throw produces an anticipated false negative. All three are retained, not fixed by host filters.
Supertype names and descendant syntax are not resolved Kotlin class identity, control flow, reachability or exception guarantees.
No iterator execution, Kotlin type-checking, collection completeness, semantic or cross-platform qualification is claimed.

six_case_plan.positive: Run the exact owner-selected syntax route on these immutable source bytes. Expected ranges are authored from the pinned predicate, never observed output.
six_case_plan.negative: Run the independent valid alternative with this SAME rule active and require an enabled upstream descriptor even with no finding.
six_case_plan.configuration: Replay original positive bytes with the selected rule explicitly disabled. This is a separately counted configuration control, never a scope/default-activation reduction.
six_case_plan.version: Replay positive bytes under the pinned CLI; require a fresh per-cohort version probe and two per-rule Common/Native abstentions. Modeled baseline 2.4.21 versus parser 2.4.10 remains unqualified.
six_case_plan.suppression: Use genuine upstream file annotation only on an additional package-isolated copy; the unsuppressed original neighbor must keep every expected range.
six_case_plan.regression: Seal the negative correction as the child of suppression, delete the obsolete suppressed copy, and verify both registered parent and child unchanged.

qualification_note: Authored ranges/intents are not observed diagnostics. Retain unexpected/false-positive outputs and all misses; never rewrite expectations to force a pass. Real isolated runner, active descriptor, source snapshots and fresh source-bound evidence require separate root admission. No natural-project, parser, semantic, ownership, cancellation-flow, model or release qualification.
